title: Transportation
content:
Transportation projects, planning, and data for Albuquerque.
This section separates long-range plans and funding from current projects, while preserving the lead agency and source date for each item. City streets, regional programs, Bernalillo County facilities, and state highways are intentionally kept distinct.
Start with Transportation Plans for the adopted regional framework and current improvement program. Use Roadway Projects, Bicycling, and Transit for mode- or corridor-specific information.

title: Housing & Land Use
content:
Housing development, zoning, and land use data.
This section combines adopted housing policy, current housing-need evidence, the legal development framework, and live activity data. A plan may describe policy and need, while a permit or project record describes a different stage of development; the pages keep those roles separate.
For the core policy and evidence, see Affordable Housing. For regulations and site research, start with Zoning & IDO and Development Process.

title: Parks & Public Works
content:
City facilities, parks, and infrastructure projects.
This section covers City parks, facilities, and capital work, with clearly labeled County data when it provides useful regional context. It does not duplicate current project trackers; those stay linked to the agencies that maintain schedules and project attributes.
See Parks & Recreation, City Facilities, and Capital Projects.

title: City Data
content:
City budget, spending, and demographic data.
Use this section for the City’s adopted budget and capital program, alongside maintained data about people, neighborhoods, public safety, and public records. Live datasets are linked to their publishers; permanent adopted records are preserved in the document library.
Start with Budget & Spending, Capital Spending, and Demographics.

title: Design References
content:
Reference drawings, engineering details, and technical guidance related to transportation infrastructure and street design.
Regional reference index#MRMPO transportation reference material
MRCOG’s maintained reference index connects regional practitioners to current complete-streets and multimodal design resources from recognized national transportation organizations, complementing locally adopted standards without duplicating third-party publications.
NMDOT Quick Build Guide#Reference guidance for quick-build transportation and multimodal safety projects.
NMDOT Quick Build Guide Introduces quick-build project planning, design, materials, public engagement, installation, and evaluation practices for delivering lower-cost multimodal safety improvements on New Mexico streets. Toronto-style “Tall Curbs” for Bike Lane Protection#High-profile concrete curb barriers used for physical separation and protection of bicycle lanes and other multimodal facilities.
Toronto-style Tall Curb Engineering Drawings Provides engineering drawings and dimensional details for the high-profile concrete curb units used to create physical separation between bicycle lanes and motor-vehicle traffic. Tall Curb Spec Sheet Summarizes the standard tall-curb unit’s geometry and construction specifications for designers, contractors, and reviewers planning protected bicycle-lane separation treatments on Albuquerque projects. Tall Curb End Spec Sheet Documents the geometry and construction requirements for terminal curb units, which provide a defined transition at the beginning or end of a tall-curb installation. Tall Curb Full Installation Procedures Presents the complete field-installation sequence for tall-curb barriers, including layout, pavement preparation, positioning, anchoring, and checks needed for a consistent finished installation. Tall Curb Anchor Pin Installation Guidelines Gives focused field guidance for installing the anchor pins that secure tall-curb units to pavement, supporting consistent placement and durable protected-lane installations.

title: Maps & Data
content:
Interactive maps, datasets, and dashboards are grouped here by tool rather than policy topic. A map may also appear in its substantive category—such as Bike Maps or Zoning & IDO—so it can be found from either direction without duplicating the source data.
Browse Maps for geographic reference tools and Dashboards for current project, safety, and program data.

title: ABQ Ride
content:
ABQ Ride bus service information and data.
Uptown Connect#Uptown Connect project page
Tracks the City’s transit-centered redevelopment of the Uptown Transit Center, including design and construction progress, the transit plaza, affordable and market-rate housing, commercial space, sustainability features, and the anticipated 2026–2028 delivery schedule.
ABQ RIDE: routes and schedules
The City’s current route, schedule, detour, and trip-planning information. Consult the official service page before a trip because operational details can change.
ABQ RIDE open data
The City publishes General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) data for applications and analysis. The live feed is preferable to an archived copy for current service information.

title: Affordable Housing
content:
Affordable housing programs and data.
Plans and Data#ABC Comprehensive Plan, Chapter 9: Housing (2025 Update)
The housing element of the adopted Albuquerque/Bernalillo County Comprehensive Plan sets policies for housing choice, affordability, neighborhood stability, fair housing, infrastructure, and coordinated implementation across the city and unincorporated county.
Albuquerque Region Housing Needs Assessment (2024)
Prepared for the City of Albuquerque and Mid-Region Council of Governments, this regional assessment documents current housing needs, production needs, vacant-land capacity, growth, fair-share analysis, demographic trends, and conditions affecting housing affordability across the Albuquerque region.
City of Albuquerque 2023-2027 Consolidated Plan and 2023 Action Plan
The City’s HUD Consolidated Plan identifies housing, homelessness, community-development, and fair-housing needs for 2023-2027. Its accompanying 2023 Action Plan describes the first year’s planned use of federal housing and community-development resources.

title: Bicycling
content:
Bicycle infrastructure, planning, and safety data.
The bicycle section distinguishes system plans and mapped facilities from individual projects. Current projects have active implementation material; planned projects have a formal funding or advancement signal but not yet the same implementation record; completed projects are reserved for final reference material.
Start with Bike Plans for the network framework, Bike Maps for live geographic tools, and Safety & Crash Data for City and regional safety sources.

title: Bike Maps
content:
Multi-use trails and paths in Albuquerque.
Regional long-range bikeway network#MRMPO Long-Range Bikeway System Map (2026)
Maps the adopted long-range bikeway network for the Albuquerque metropolitan planning area, distinguishing existing and proposed regional bicycle facilities used to guide coordination, project development, and future investment.
County GIS Data#Bernalillo County Bikeways
This live Bernalillo County GIS service maps county-maintained bikeways in unincorporated Bernalillo County. Use it as a current reference for facilities beyond Albuquerque city limits; the county publishes it as data, not a static map.
Bernalillo County Multi-Use Trails
This live Bernalillo County GIS service maps county-maintained multi-use trails in unincorporated areas. Motorized traffic is excluded from these trails, making the service a useful companion to local bicycle and pedestrian network maps.
MRCOG bicycle and pedestrian planning maps
MRCOG maintains regional active-transportation planning maps, counts, analyses, and a long-range bicycle system map for the Albuquerque metropolitan planning area. Use it for regional network context beyond individual City facilities.

title: Bike Plans
content:
City bicycle planning documents and master plans, including current and previous network plans and supporting materials.
Current Bike Plan#2024 Bikeway and Trail Facilities Plan Establishes Albuquerque’s current bicycle and trail network vision, policies, facility recommendations, project priorities, and implementation framework for safer, better-connected active transportation. Bicycle and Trail Crossings Guide Provides design guidance for bicycle and trail crossings, helping practitioners select treatments that improve visibility, clarify priority, and reduce conflicts at roadway intersections. Appendix A – Planning and Policy Framework Summarizes the adopted plans, policies, and regulatory context that shaped the 2024 plan’s goals, network recommendations, priorities, and implementation approach. Appendix B – Community Survey Summary (Spring 2023) Reports responses from the spring 2023 community survey, documenting residents’ bicycling and trail experiences, concerns, priorities, and desired improvements across Albuquerque. Appendix C – Project Priorities Survey Map Results (Fall 2023) Compiles mapped results from the fall 2023 priorities survey, showing where participants identified desired bikeway, crossing, connection, and trail improvements. Appendix D – Bikeway Evaluation Process Explains the plan’s repeatable method for evaluating proposed bikeways, comparing corridor conditions, network needs, feasibility, and project priorities across Albuquerque. Appendix E – Bike Boulevard Toolkit Describes planning and design tools for low-stress bicycle boulevards, including traffic calming, crossing improvements, wayfinding, and strategies for managing motor-vehicle volumes. Appendix F – Priority Projects Tables (Jan 2025) Lists the plan’s priority bicycle and trail projects as of January 2025, organizing recommended improvements for implementation and future programming. Appendix G – Project Profiles Presents detailed profiles for selected priority projects, describing corridor needs, recommended facilities, implementation considerations, and each project’s role in the network. Appendix H – Multiuse Trail Considerations (2015 Plan) Preserves relevant multiuse-trail planning and design considerations from the 2015 plan for continued technical reference alongside the updated 2024 recommendations. Appendix I – Bollard Assessment (2013) Documents the City’s 2013 assessment of multiuse-trail bollards, including operational and safety considerations that inform decisions about access-control treatments on trails. Previous Bike Plans#2015 Bikeways and Trails Facilities Plan The previous adopted facilities plan established the bicycle and trail network, policies, design guidance, and project priorities that preceded the current 2024 plan. 2011 Albuquerque Bikeways and Trails Master Plan Update Updated Albuquerque’s earlier bicycle and trail planning framework, documenting existing conditions, proposed networks, facility guidance, and implementation priorities at that time. 2000 Albuquerque Comprehensive On-Street Bicycle Plan Established a citywide framework for Albuquerque’s on-street bicycle facilities, identifying network needs, recommended routes, design approaches, policies, and implementation priorities. 1993 Trails and Bikeways Facility Plan Documents Albuquerque’s early citywide approach to developing connected trail and bikeway facilities, preserving the historical basis for subsequent network planning. Related Bicycle Policy#City Council Resolution R-07-268: Bike Boulevards (2007) Designates Mountain Road, Silver Avenue, and 14th Street bike-boulevard routes; appropriates up to $400,000 for design, engineering, and initial implementation; and directs amendments to the Comprehensive Bikeway Facilities Plan.

title: Budget & Spending
content:
City budget and expenditure data.
Current Budget#City of Albuquerque Approved Budget, Fiscal Year 2027
The City of Albuquerque’s adopted Fiscal Year 2027 budget provides citywide revenue, appropriations, department and program details, capital support, performance information, and summary charts explaining where public funds come from and how they are allocated.

title: Capital Projects
content:
Public works capital improvement projects.
Current project data#Municipal Development featured projects
The City’s maintained index highlights major transportation, facility, safety, parks, and public-space capital projects, providing an accessible project gateway while the machine-readable project-data endpoint is unavailable.
Municipal Development project data
This maintained City dataset is the starting point for current Municipal Development projects. It is intentionally linked live because capital-project schedules, scopes, and statuses are subject to change.
2025 General Obligation Bond Approved Program Book
The City’s adopted bond program is cataloged in City Data and is cross-linked here because it is an important source of public-works capital funding. The document is stored once, not duplicated.

title: Capital Spending
content:
Capital improvement spending and projects.
Capital Program#2025 General Obligation Bond Approved Program Book
Albuquerque’s approved 2025 General Obligation Bond program describes proposed capital investments across the 2025-2034 decade plan, including project scopes, funding categories, public facilities, infrastructure, and implementation priorities.

title: City Facilities
content:
City buildings and facilities.
Public-facility references#Accessible City park and recreation facilities
The City identifies accessible parks, recreation facilities, and programs, with an accompanying location map. It is a maintained public-facing resource rather than a static facilities inventory.

title: Completed Projects
content: Completed bicycle infrastructure projects.

title: Completed Projects
content: Completed roadway projects and related final documents.

title: Current Projects
content:
Currently active bicycle infrastructure projects.
Buena Vista Bike Boulevard#Location: Buena Vista Dr SE, from Central Ave SE to Gibson Blvd SE
Buena Vista Bike Boulevard 60% Plans Shows the 60-percent design for bicycle-boulevard improvements along Buena Vista Drive, including traffic-calming, crossing, signing, pavement-marking, and corridor layout details. Questions or comments email Paul Olson at DMD polson@cabq.gov
Moon Street Cycletrack / Bike Boulevard#Location: Moon Street NE, between Academy Rd NE and Spain Rd NE
Moon St NE Cycletrack Plans Documents the planned Moon Street restriping and cycletrack layout between Academy and Spain, including bicycle facilities, lane configuration, markings, and intersection treatments. Questions or comments email Melissa Roseman at DMD melissaroseman@cabq.gov

title: Current Projects
content:
Active roadway projects, near-term implementation work, and project documents.
Unser Boulevard and Paseo del Norte#Unser and Paseo project website
Tracks construction of Albuquerque’s $62 million Unser Boulevard and Paseo del Norte widening project, including traffic control, schedules, lane expansion, bicycle and trail connections, lighting, and stormwater improvements.
I-25 Improved: Comanche to Montgomery#I-25 Improved project website
Provides current construction phasing, traffic shifts, closures, detour maps, alerts, and contact information for NMDOT’s reconstruction of I-25, frontage roads, bridges, and interchanges between Comanche and Montgomery.
Broadway Boulevard Road Diet#Engineering Drawings: Coal to MLK Provides engineering drawings for the Broadway Boulevard road-diet segment from Coal Avenue to Martin Luther King Jr. Avenue, including lane layout, striping, and related improvements. Draft Engineering Drawings: MLK to Lomas Shows the draft road-diet design from Martin Luther King Jr. Avenue to Lomas Boulevard, documenting proposed lane configuration, striping, and intersection details. Cost Estimate: MLK to Lomas Presents the 60-percent design cost estimate for the Broadway segment between Martin Luther King Jr. Avenue and Lomas Boulevard, organized by anticipated construction items. Traffic Evaluation (Signed July 2, 2025) Evaluates traffic operations and engineering considerations for the proposed Broadway Boulevard road diet, providing the signed technical basis for the project’s lane changes. Citywide construction maps#Permitted construction in the public right of way
The City’s regularly updated map shows permitted right-of-way construction, locations, dates, descriptions, and responsible contractors, helping residents distinguish current City-jurisdiction work from state and emergency projects.
Construction moratoriums
Lists current event and seasonal construction moratoriums, affected street boundaries, downloadable maps, dates, and the live map used to coordinate safe traffic operations during major Albuquerque events.

title: Dashboards
content:
Data dashboards and visualizations.
Project, program, and safety dashboards#Permitted construction in the public right of way
The City’s regularly updated map shows permitted right-of-way construction, locations, dates, descriptions, and responsible contractors. It is cross-listed under Current Roadway Projects for people tracking active work.
Construction moratoriums
Maps current event and seasonal construction restrictions, affected street boundaries, and effective dates. It is cross-listed under Current Roadway Projects because the restrictions directly affect construction scheduling.
City Municipal Development project data
The City’s maintained project dataset provides a direct way to explore Municipal Development projects and their available attributes. It is preferable to a copied project list that can quickly become outdated.
Pedestrian, bicyclist, and traffic-safety projects map
This City map points to the current geographic view of safety projects. It is also linked from the bicycle-safety section because the same live source serves both purposes.
NMDOT Project Dashboard
NMDOT’s statewide dashboard is useful for tracking state highway work affecting Albuquerque. Use the accompanying project pages for the record of a particular study or corridor.
NMDOT STIP viewer
The Statewide Transportation Improvement Program viewer is the current source for programmed transportation projects. It complements, but does not replace, the regional MRCOG Transportation Improvement Program.
MRCOG traffic flow maps and busiest intersections
MRCOG provides current and historical regional traffic counts, annual weekday traffic maps, vehicle-miles-traveled information, and an interactive traffic-flow map for the Albuquerque metropolitan planning area.

title: Demographics
content:
Albuquerque demographic and census data.
Regional data#MRCOG socioeconomic data
Mid-Region Council of Governments publishes regional population, households, employment, income, commuting, and related planning data. It is the appropriate regional source when a question extends beyond City limits.
Albuquerque neighborhood data
The City’s open-data service provides neighborhood geography and associated data resources for map-based analysis, local reference, and comparisons among Albuquerque communities.

title: Development Process
content:
Cross-cutting development process documents, manuals, and reference materials.
Development Process Manual#Development Process Manual (June 2, 2020) Provides the City’s technical requirements and procedures for planning, designing, reviewing, permitting, and constructing public infrastructure associated with development projects.

title: Homeless Services
content:
Homeless services and shelter data.
Current resources and transparency#Emergency shelters, day shelters, and street outreach
The City maintains this service directory for emergency overnight shelter, day shelter, and street-outreach options. Availability and intake requirements can change; the page directs people needing help to call 311 or the relevant provider.
Shelter resources and encampment transparency
This City page links current shelter-resource information, the Shelter Connect dashboard, and publicly reported encampment-response data. Reported locations are not a substitute for on-the-ground verification.

title: Housing Pipeline
content:
Current and planned housing development projects.
Uptown Connect#Uptown Connect project page
Documents the mixed-use redevelopment planned at the Uptown Transit Center, including affordable and market-rate housing, commercial space, transit access, project stages, renderings, and the anticipated 2026–2028 construction schedule.
Development activity data#Building permits open data
The City’s maintained building-permit data is the most useful general-purpose source for recent development activity. A permit is not the same as a completed home, occupancy, affordability commitment, or project delivery date.

title: Maps
content:
Interactive maps of city data and infrastructure.
Citywide reference maps#Regional long-range transportation maps#MRMPO Bikeway System Map (2026)
MRMPO Pedestrian System Map (2026)
MRMPO Roadway System Map (2026)
MRMPO Transit System Map (2026)
These adopted regional maps show the existing and proposed long-range networks used by MRMPO to coordinate bicycle, pedestrian, roadway, and transit planning across the Albuquerque metropolitan area.
City maps for the public
The City’s map library includes the official Zone Atlas, address and parcel reference tools, council districts, land use, streets, neighborhoods, and printable maps.
Open Space maps
Albuquerque Open Space maintains access and trail maps for its lands and trailheads. Individual trail maps are available from the same City source when a printable field reference is useful.
City open-data catalog
This is the maintained entry point for City datasets, including building permits, capital projects, transit data, parks, trails, public safety, and environmental information.
County Planning Map#Bernalillo County Comprehensive Plan Development Areas
This live Bernalillo County GIS service maps development areas in the unincorporated county covered by the adopted Albuquerque/Bernalillo County Comprehensive Plan. It supports interactive viewing and structured geographic data access through the county’s public map service.

title: Micromobility
content: Bike share, scooter share, and other micromobility services.

title: Parks & Recreation
content:
Parks and recreation facilities and programs.
Plans and Data#ABC Comprehensive Plan, Chapter 10: Parks & Open Space (2025 Update)
The parks and open space element of the adopted Albuquerque/Bernalillo County Comprehensive Plan provides policy direction for park access, recreation, trail connections, conservation, stewardship, and an integrated open-space network.
Bernalillo County Open Space Holdings
This live Bernalillo County GIS service maps county real-estate holdings, including open space, parks and recreation facilities, public-safety facilities, and other county properties. It is maintained as data rather than a static downloadable document.
City Open Space planning projects and resource-management plans
Albuquerque maintains this library for project-specific Open Space plans, including trails, natural areas, visitor-use management, habitat, and facility planning. Individual records are added only when their scope is independently useful beyond this maintained library.

title: Planned Projects
content: Funded, programmed, or formally advancing bicycle projects that are not yet accompanied by active implementation materials.

title: Projects
content:
Bicycle infrastructure projects.
Project pages are organized by the strongest available status evidence, not by an assumed construction schedule. Each entry should identify its corridor, lead agency, dated source material, and whether it is active, planned, or complete.
Use Current Projects for work with current implementation material, Planned Projects for formally advancing work, and Completed Projects for final records.

title: Public Safety Data
content:
Police, fire, and emergency services data.
Current dashboards and datasets#ABQ Safety Dashboard
The City dashboard brings together public-safety measures and reporting in one maintained location. Use it for current, high-level performance information rather than treating a downloaded snapshot as current.
Police incidents open data
The City publishes police-incident data and machine-readable formats through its open-data service. Definitions, update timing, and appropriate use are described with the dataset.
Albuquerque Community Safety Department overview
The City describes the non-police response services, programs, performance role, and public contacts administered by the Albuquerque Community Safety Department throughout Albuquerque.

title: Rail Runner
content:
Rail Runner commuter rail information.
Rail Runner schedules
Rio Metro is the authoritative source for current New Mexico Rail Runner schedules and service information. Use it for travel planning rather than a static timetable.

title: Roadway Projects
content:
Street and roadway infrastructure projects.
Project status is organized deliberately: Current Projects are active or accompanied by current implementation materials; Studies are alternatives analysis or project-development work; Completed Projects retain final reference material. State highway projects are included only when they materially affect Albuquerque.
State highway project gateway#NMDOT District 3
District 3 is NMDOT’s Albuquerque-area office and the authoritative starting point for state-highway contacts, construction information, maintenance responsibilities, and district projects affecting the metropolitan area.

title: Safety & Crash Data
content:
Bicycle safety statistics and crash data.
Safety program and project map#Albuquerque Vision Zero
The City’s Vision Zero program page is the maintained source for its traffic-safety approach, performance work, and related materials. It is broader than bicycling, but directly relevant to bicycle safety and street design.
Pedestrian, bicyclist, and traffic-safety projects map
Use this City map to see the geographic context of current safety projects. It is also listed in Maps & Dashboards so visitors looking by tool rather than topic can find the same maintained source.
MRCOG Regional Transportation Safety Action Plan (2024)
MRCOG’s adopted plan uses regional crash analysis, a Safe System approach, safety strategies, area profiles, and project recommendations to address bicycle, pedestrian, roadway, and transit safety.
MRCOG safety hub
Maintains regional transportation-safety resources, including the action plan’s supporting maps, appendices, analysis, and materials covering bicycle, pedestrian, transit, and roadway safety.

title: Speed Management
content:
Traffic calming and speed management initiatives.
Neighborhood Traffic Management Program#Program FAQ and evaluation criteria
Albuquerque’s Neighborhood Traffic Management Program explains how local streets are evaluated for traffic-calming measures, the role of community participation, and the criteria used to prioritize work.
Program documents and traffic-calming tools
The City provides the program policy, toolkit, and individual traffic-calming reference documents. These are a better source for process and design choices than isolated project announcements.
Vision Zero implementation work
The Vision Zero implementation page provides the City’s broader safety-program context, including traffic management, automated speed enforcement, and active safety work.

title: Studies
content:
Transportation studies and reports.
State highway studies affecting Albuquerque#I-40 West Corridor Study Executive Summary (2024)
This NMDOT executive summary covers the I-40 Phase I-A/B corridor study from Arizona to Albuquerque, mileposts 0 through 150. The NMDOT project page remains the source for project updates and supporting materials.
I-40 Phase I-A/B Corridor Study (2024)
Presents NMDOT’s signed Phase I-A/B analysis of I-40 from Arizona to Albuquerque, documenting public involvement, existing conditions, traffic and safety, alternatives screening, preferred improvements, costs, operational enhancements, and implementation.
I-40 Highway Operations Improvement Plan (2024)
Provides NMDOT’s 25-year implementation roadmap for I-40 from Arizona to Albuquerque’s Atrisco Vista interchange, covering preferred improvements, design guidance, maintenance, incident management, priority projects, and phasing.
I-40 Conceptual Alternatives Plan Sheets (2024)
Contains 139 preliminary plan sheets mapping conceptual I-40 improvements from Arizona to Albuquerque, including reconstruction limits, typical sections, crossovers, bridge constraints, curves, ramps, and pavement conditions.
Big I Operations Study
NMDOT’s Big I study page describes work at the I-25/I-40 interchange and links to the project’s interactive material. It belongs under studies until a defined implementation project and status are established.
I-25 S-Curve Area Study
Documents NMDOT’s evaluation of safety and mobility improvements between Avenida Cesar Chavez and Lomas Boulevard, including alignment alternatives, interchange concepts, screening results, public meetings, and draft recommendations.
I-25 Gibson Interchange Reconstruction Project
Tracks design development for replacing the Gibson interchange and improving I-25 between Sunport and Avenida Cesar Chavez, including braided ramps, frontage roads, multimodal connections, environmental review, and public materials.
I-25 Bobby Foster and Mesa del Sol Interchange Study
Covers NMDOT’s Phase I-A/B study of I-25 from the Rio Grande bridges to Sunport Boulevard, evaluating future interchange, corridor, access, safety, and capacity improvements serving Mesa del Sol.
NM 556/Tramway Boulevard Public Engagement Summary (November 2025)
Summarizes NMDOT’s 2025 public engagement for NM 556/Tramway Boulevard, including meeting outreach, roughly 180 comments, recurring safety and operations concerns, agency responses, and next steps.
NMDOT NM 556/Tramway Boulevard Corridor Study
Tracks the active Albuquerque corridor study from Central Avenue to Live Oak Road, including current findings, April 2026 meeting resources, safety priorities, recommended strategies, and the study timeline.

title: Submit Documents
content:
Submit documents#Email info [at] abqinfo [dot] com to submit documentation to the site.
Information that is not available on cabq.gov or other public sites is prioritized.
For easiest transmission, upload documents to your Google Drive, set sharing to Anyone with the link, and send the link.

title: Sun Van
content:
Sun Van paratransit service information.
City paratransit service
Albuquerque’s official page for Sun Van and related paratransit information, including current eligibility, reservations, service policies, accessibility guidance, and rider resources.

title: Transit
content:
Public transit services and data.
Use the service pages for current rider information and the Transportation Plans section for regional transit planning. Schedules, fares, alerts, and eligibility rules change frequently, so this site links to the agencies that maintain them rather than duplicating them.
Statewide planning context#Connect New Mexico: Statewide Public Transportation Plan (May 2025)
NMDOT’s final statewide public transportation plan establishes the broader policy and investment context for transit providers, riders, and connections affecting Albuquerque. It supplements local and regional plans; it does not replace ABQ RIDE or MRCOG service and programming sources.

title: Transportation Plans
content:
Regional plans, long-range plans, and other system-level transportation planning documents.
Regional Transportation Planning#ABC Comprehensive Plan, Chapter 6: Transportation (2025 Update)
The transportation element of the adopted Albuquerque/Bernalillo County Comprehensive Plan guides land use and mobility decisions, covering a multimodal system, safe access, travel choices, coordination, and implementation policies for the city and unincorporated county.
MRMPO 2045 Metropolitan Transportation Plan
MRMPO 2045 Metropolitan Transportation Plan - Full Appendix
2026 Long-Range Transportation System Maps#Pedestrian System Map
Maps the Albuquerque metropolitan area’s adopted long-range pedestrian network, identifying existing and proposed pedestrian-priority facilities that support regional planning, project development, and implementation beyond the 2045 planning horizon.
Roadway System Map
Maps the adopted long-range roadway network for the Albuquerque metropolitan planning area, including existing and proposed major facilities used to coordinate growth, investment, project development, and regional connectivity.
Transit System Map
Maps the adopted long-range transit network for the Albuquerque metropolitan area, showing existing services and proposed high-capacity or expanded connections that guide coordinated transit planning beyond the 2045 horizon.
MRMPO Transportation Improvement Program, FFY 2024-2029
The current Mid-Region MPO Transportation Improvement Program lists federally funded transportation projects scheduled across fiscal years 2024-2029, including budgets, phases, lead agencies, funding sources, and status for roadway, transit, bicycle, pedestrian, and other work.
MRMPO performance-based planning and programming
MRCOG’s maintained performance hub gathers the regional measures and current reports used to set targets, track safety and system performance, and coordinate transit asset-management and public-transportation safety planning.
MRMPO Unified Planning Work Program, FFY 2027-2028
Defines MRMPO’s federally required transportation planning work and budget for FFY 2027-2028, covering administration, TIP management, data, metropolitan planning, safety, active transportation, ABQ RIDE, Rio Metro, and imagery.
Statewide Programming#NMDOT Statewide Transportation Improvement Program
NMDOT’s maintained STIP page provides the current statewide program and amendment materials for federally funded transportation projects, including projects and funding actions affecting Albuquerque.
Development Process#Development Process Manual (June 2, 2020) Provides the City’s technical requirements and procedures for planning, designing, reviewing, permitting, and constructing public infrastructure associated with development projects.

title: Zoning & IDO
content:
Zoning regulations and Integrated Development Ordinance information.
Current ordinance and zoning tools#Integrated Development Ordinance — effective May 6, 2026
The City’s current Integrated Development Ordinance establishes zoning, development standards, and review procedures for Albuquerque. This preserved original is the effective May 2026 release; the City IDO page retains archived updates and legislative history.
Interactive IDO zoning map
Search an address or parcel and inspect the mapped zoning layer. Map results should be checked against the effective IDO and City review staff for a site-specific determination.
City zoning and land-use maps
The City’s public map library includes the Zone Atlas, address atlas, council districts, land use, neighborhood associations, and printable reference maps.
